recommendations.source_detail: sql:over_provisioned_executors ref=0: companion min-executor floor to accompany maxExecutors change; anti-pattern fence requires minExecutors ≥ 1 when dynamic allocation is enabled
recommendations.rationale: Dynamic allocation is enabled (dynamic_allocation_enabled=true) and minExecutors is currently 0. The anti-pattern fence requires that whenever maxExecutors is set, minExecutors must also be set to ≥ 1 to prevent cold-start with 0 executors. This is a companion safety change to the maxExecutors reduction (priority 2). Setting minExecutors=1 ensures the job always has at least one executor available at startup. Cost impact is negligible (one executor floor vs. zero).
recommendations.explanation: Dynamic allocation is active (dynamic_allocation_enabled=true) with minExecutors currently confirmed at 0 (source: task_profile) and maxExecutors set to 1,200. When the cluster scales down to zero executors between task waves, the next wave must wait for fresh executor allocation before any work can begin — a cold-start stall that directly inflates wall-clock duration. Setting minExecutors=1 guarantees at least one executor is always warm and ready, eliminating that startup gap without meaningfully changing resource consumption.
recommendations.expected_impact: Eliminates cold-start executor wait at job startup; the idle_ratio for this run is 7.8%, so the recoverable idle time is bounded by that fraction of allocated time — the actual gain from this single floor change will be a small subset of that, but the protection against zero-executor stalls is categorical.
recommendations.risk_note: Holding one executor alive continuously adds a negligible, fixed cost (one executor out of a max of 1,200), but there is no functional risk.

recommendations.source_detail: agent_discovered ref=2: Spill Trending Sharply Upward — Partition Count Likely Exhausted
recommendations.rationale: Disk spill has grown +79% over 20 runs (3.2 GB → 5.7 GB latest, 20-run mean 1.8 GB) with zero config changes, indicating quietly growing input data volume inflating per-task working sets. AQE is currently OFF (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled is unset, defaulting to false on this YARN cluster), so the static 11,000-partition shuffle is the binding runtime count. With AQE enabled, Spark will dynamically coalesce or split shuffle partitions at runtime, shrinking per-task data size as input volume grows — the lowest-risk first lever for the spill trajectory. This is a health-remedy recommendation; it does not increase cost. The current run spilled 2.04 GB to disk and 70.8 GB from memory, all attributed to Stage 2 (29,861-task read+aggregate). The spill_ratio for this run is 0.000299 — below the 10% health-gate threshold — but the monotonically increasing trend across 20 runs makes this a proactive health fix before the gate opens. Annual task cost baseline: $319,538. Enabling AQE has no direct cost impact (no resource allocation change); saving_fraction is not set as the cost direction is neutral.
recommendations.explanation: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled is unset (confirmed not_set, defaulting to false on this YARN cluster), so the static shuffle partition count of 11,000 is applied uniformly at every stage regardless of actual data volume. Disk spill has grown +79.3% over 20 runs (first run: 3.17 GB, latest run: 5.68 GB, 20-run mean: 1.81 GB) with a monotonically increasing trend and no config changes, indicating that growing input data is inflating per-task working sets against a fixed partition count. Enabling AQE allows Spark to coalesce small shuffle partitions and split oversized ones at runtime, directly reducing the per-task data volume that is currently overflowing executor memory and landing on disk (this run: 2.04 GB disk spill, spill_ratio=0.000299).
recommendations.expected_impact: AQE cannot be arithmetically mapped to a cost saving fraction (no resource allocation changes), but by dynamically right-sizing partitions it is expected to slow or reverse the spill growth trajectory — the current run's disk spill of 2.04 GB sits at the 70th percentile of the 20-run baseline, and without intervention the trend projects continued growth toward the health-gate threshold.
recommendations.risk_note: AQE's partition coalescing can occasionally produce unexpectedly large merged partitions if skew is severe; with skew_ratio=0.237 on this run, monitor per-task peak memory after enabling to confirm no new OOM pressure.

blocked_recommendations.rationale: The SQL rule detected over-provisioned executors with an estimated annual saving of $44,723. vcore_utilization=0.572 and idle_ratio=0.078 confirm meaningful executor idle time. Skew_ratio=0.237 is also below the 0.30 conflict threshold, so the skew anti-pattern guard does not apply. The SQL engine's suggested ceiling of 618 (from 1200) is a 48.5% reduction. Per the conservative-step fence, a single-step 48.5% cut is aggressive; however, the SQL rule's sizing is based on observed peak active executors with a 30% headroom margin — this is the deterministic safe floor. The saving estimate from the tool: cutting maxExecutors 1200→618 yields an estimated saving fraction of 0.485 (upper bound assuming the job runs at ceiling; real saving is lower when the ceiling is rarely hit). The idle_ratio of 0.078 provides a floor anchor: at minimum ~7.8% of executor-time is idle, supporting a meaningful reduction. Anchoring conservatively to idle_ratio: estimated_saving_fraction = 0.078 (the directly measured idle waste share). blocked_by: Active disk spill detected (0% of shuffle I/O) — reducing executor count removes the memory capacity needed to keep shuffle data in-memory. Resolve spill first (increase spark.sql.shuffle.partitions or executor memory).

unactioned_insights.title: Executor GC Monotonically Increasing Over 20 Runs — Proactive Memory Warning
unactioned_insights.description: Executor JVM GC time has increased monotonically over the last 20 runs (+9.3% first-to-last, current run at 86,952 seconds of fleet GC time, in the 80th percentile of the baseline). Critically, memory headroom is only 11.2% — well below the 20% fragility threshold — while gc_pressure is 5.6% (below the SQL rule threshold of 20%, so no SQL rule fired). This combination — moderate GC pressure + very tight memory headroom + active spill — is the precursor signature for a GC health event. The job is not in GC thrash today, but the trajectory is clear: as input volume grows (evidenced by the spill trend), the heap will be squeezed further and GC pressure will cross the health threshold. The GC collector in use is PS MarkSweep / PS Scavenge (parallel collector, confirmed from executor events), which is known to degrade non-linearly on heaps above ~16 GB under high allocation pressure.
unactioned_insights.reason: Executor GC monotonically increasing (ref=3): gc_pressure=0.056 (5.6%) is below the 12% health-gate threshold and below the 10% action threshold. The suggested action is to monitor for 3–5 more runs and only act if gc_pressure crosses 10%. No config change is warranted this visit — the insight explicitly states 'do not right-size executor memory downward while this trend is open', and no upsize is justified while gc_pressure has not crossed the health threshold. The AQE enablement (priority 1) addresses the root cause (growing per-task working sets) and is expected to relieve GC pressure indirectly. The GC collector switch (spark.executor.extraJavaOptions=-XX:+UseG1GC) is not a valid config_key in the approved key registry and cannot be recommended this visit; it should be revisited if gc_pressure crosses 10% after AQE is enabled.

This is a health-tier signal: efficiency right-sizing (including the SQL-detected over_provisioned_executors insight) should be deferred until spill is resolved.

Stage 2 metrics confirm: internal.metrics.diskBytesSpilled=2,037,760,607, internal.metrics.memoryBytesSpilled=70,766,297,088. spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=NOT_SET (false). spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=11000 (static, unchanged across 20 runs). executor_heap_memory=16 GB, executor_memory=20 GB, executor_cores=7 (per-slot heap ≈ 16/7 ≈ 2.3 GB).
tier4.suggested_action: Enable AQE (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true) so Spark can dynamically right-size shuffle partitions at runtime. With AQE off and a static 11,000-partition shuffle, per-task data size grows directly with input volume. Enabling AQE is the lowest-risk first step; it will also make the static spark.sql.shuffle.partitions value advisory rather than binding. If spill persists after enabling AQE, investigate whether executor_cores=7 is creating excessive memory contention per slot (per-slot execution memory ≈ 2.3 GB heap / 7 cores ≈ 330 MB, which is very tight for a wide-schema 180-column Parquet aggregation).

tier4.identifier: Executor GC Monotonically Increasing Over 20 Runs — Proactive Memory Warning
tier4.title: Executor GC Monotonically Increasing Over 20 Runs — Proactive Memory Warning
tier4.description: Executor JVM GC time has increased monotonically over the last 20 runs (+9.3% first-to-last, current run at 86,952 seconds of fleet GC time, in the 80th percentile of the baseline). Critically, memory headroom is only 11.2% — well below the 20% fragility threshold — while gc_pressure is 5.6% (below the SQL rule threshold of 20%, so no SQL rule fired). This combination — moderate GC pressure + very tight memory headroom + active spill — is the precursor signature for a GC health event. The job is not in GC thrash today, but the trajectory is clear: as input volume grows (evidenced by the spill trend), the heap will be squeezed further and GC pressure will cross the health threshold. The GC collector in use is PS MarkSweep / PS Scavenge (parallel collector, confirmed from executor events), which is known to degrade non-linearly on heaps above ~16 GB under high allocation pressure.
tier4.evidence: executors__jvm_gc_time trend over 20 runs: mean=75,570s, current=86,952s (80th percentile, z=1.05, band=ELEVATED), trend=INCREASING +9.3%. memory_headroom=0.112 (11.2%, below 20% fragility threshold). gc_pressure=0.056 (5.6%, below SQL threshold of 20%). has_spill=true. executor_heap_memory=16 GB. GC collector from executor events payload: 'gcType': 'PS MarkSweep,PS Scavenge'. Stage 4 task-level jvmGcTime distribution: p25=3,614ms, p50=6,640ms, p75=8,209ms, max=12,746ms per task.
tier4.suggested_action: Monitor gc_pressure across the next 3–5 runs. If the increasing trend continues, the primary lever is enabling AQE (see spill insight above) to reduce per-task working set size. If GC pressure crosses 10% after AQE is enabled, consider switching the GC collector from PS MarkSweep to G1GC via spark.executor.extraJavaOptions=-XX:+UseG1GC, which handles large heaps with high object churn significantly better than the parallel collector. Do not right-size executor memory downward while this trend is open.

tier4.identifier: Stage 2 Skew: Max Task Duration 13× the P75 — Speculative Execution Not Enabled
tier4.title: Stage 2 Skew: Max Task Duration 13× the P75 — Speculative Execution Not Enabled
tier4.description: Stage 2 (the 29,861-task read+aggregate stage) shows a confirmed skew event: average task duration 12s, P75=13s, but max=164s — a 13× ratio between the worst task and the 75th percentile. This is the stage responsible for all spill. The skew event was captured in the run's insight events. Speculative execution (spark.speculation) is not configured, meaning the straggler task runs to completion without a parallel speculative attempt, directly extending Stage 2's wall-clock time. The skew_ratio for the run is 0.237 (just below the 0.25 SQL threshold, so no SQL rule fired). With 29,861 tasks and 2,137 executors, a single 164-second straggler at the tail of the stage adds measurable latency. The skew is input-side (FileSourceScanExec reading 215,783 Parquet files across 93 input paths), suggesting uneven file sizes rather than a data-value hot key.

tier4.suggested_action: Investigate whether the 215,783 input Parquet files have highly uneven sizes (a few very large files dominate). If so, compact or repartition the input data to produce more uniform file sizes. As a complementary measure, enabling AQE (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true) will also activate AQE's skew-join handling for shuffle stages. Do not enable spark.speculation as a primary fix — it doubles resource consumption for the straggler task and masks the root cause.
